item_name: Impact on Resident — Did any of the identified symptom(s) put the resident at significant risk for physical illness or injury?

lookback_source.quote: Consider the previous review of the medical record, staff interviews across all shifts and disciplines, interviews with others who had close interactions with the resident and previous observations of the behaviors identified in E0200 for the 7-day look-back period.

lookback_notes: The Steps for Assessment for E0500 direct the assessor to consider the behaviors identified in E0200 for the 7-day look-back period. The document does not state on this page how the 7 days are counted relative to the ARD.

coding_levels.label: No
coding_levels.definition: None of the identified behavioral symptom(s) placed the resident at clinically significant risk for a physical illness or injury.

source.quote: Code 0, no: if none of the identified behavioral symptom(s) placed the resident at clinically significant risk for a physical illness or injury.

coding_levels.label: Yes
coding_levels.definition: Any of the identified behavioral symptom(s) placed the resident at clinically significant risk for a physical illness or injury, even if no injury occurred.

source.quote: Code 1, yes: if any of the identified behavioral symptom(s) placed the resident at clinically significant risk for a physical illness or injury, even if no injury occurred.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code E0500A (along with E0500B and E0500C) based on all of the behavioral symptoms coded in E0200.

source.quote: Code E0500A, E0500B, and E0500C based on all of the behavioral symptoms coded in E0200.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Determine whether the behaviors coded in E0200 put the resident at significant risk of physical illness or injury.

source.quote: Determine whether those behaviors put the resident at significant risk of physical illness or injury, whether the behaviors significantly interfered with the resident's care, and/or whether the behaviors significantly interfered with the resident's participation in activities or social interactions.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code 0, no, if none of the identified behavioral symptom(s) placed the resident at clinically significant risk for a physical illness or injury.

source.quote: Code 0, no: if none of the identified behavioral symptom(s) placed the resident at clinically significant risk for a physical illness or injury.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code 1, yes, if any of the identified behavioral symptom(s) placed the resident at clinically significant risk for a physical illness or injury; an actual injury need not have occurred.

source.quote: Code 1, yes: if any of the identified behavioral symptom(s) placed the resident at clinically significant risk for a physical illness or injury, even if no injury occurred.

federal_coding_rules.rule: For E0500A, code based on whether the risk for physical injury or illness is known to occur commonly under similar circumstances (i.e., with residents who exhibit similar behavior in a similar environment). Physical injury is trauma that results in pain or other distressing physical symptoms, impaired organ function, physical disability, or other adverse consequences, regardless of the need for medical, surgical, nursing, or rehabilitative intervention.

source.quote: For E0500A, code based on whether the risk for physical injury or illness is known to occur commonly under similar circumstances (i.e., with residents who exhibit similar behavior in a similar environment). Physical injury is trauma that results in pain or other distressing physical symptoms, impaired organ function, physical disability, or other adverse consequences, regardless of the need for medical, surgical, nursing, or rehabilitative intervention.

federal_coding_rules.rule: E0500 is completed only when E0300 is coded 1, yes (i.e., any of E0200A, E0200B, or E0200C were coded 1, 2, or 3); if E0200A, E0200B, and E0200C are all coded 0, E0300 is coded 0 and the assessor skips to E0800, so E0500 is not completed.

source.quote: Code 1, yes: if any of E0200A, E0200B, or E0200C were coded 1, 2, or 3. Proceed to complete Impact on Resident item (E0500), and Impact on Others item (E0600).

federal_coding_rules.rule: When E0300 is coded 0 (no behavioral symptoms in E0200), skip to E0800, Rejection of Care—Presence & Frequency, rather than completing E0500.

source.quote: Code 0, no: if E0200A, E0200B, and E0200C all are coded 0, not present. Skip to Rejection of Care—Presence & Frequency item (E0800).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Resident intent should not be taken into account when coding items in Section E.

source.quote: Resident intent should not be taken into account when coding for items in this section.

federal.criterion: Review of the medical record for the 7-day look-back period supporting the behaviors identified in E0200 and their impact on the resident.

source.quote: Consider the previous review of the medical record, staff interviews across all shifts and disciplines, interviews with others who had close interactions with the resident and previous observations of the behaviors identified in E0200 for the 7-day look-back period.

federal.notes: Framed as a Step for Assessment rather than an explicit documentation requirement.

federal.criterion: Staff interviews across all shifts and disciplines, and interviews with others who had close interactions with the resident, plus observations of the behaviors identified in E0200.

source.quote: Consider the previous review of the medical record, staff interviews across all shifts and disciplines, interviews with others who had close interactions with the resident and previous observations of the behaviors identified in E0200 for the 7-day look-back period.

federal.notes: Same Steps for Assessment passage; cited as the source of information supporting the code.

federal.criterion: Assessment and documentation can be compared to a baseline to identify changes in the resident's behavior, including response to interventions.

source.quote: Subsequent assessments and documentation can be compared to a baseline to identify changes in the resident's behavior, including response to interventions.

federal.notes: Stated under Planning for Care as rationale, not as a coding requirement.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied pages do not tie E0500A to any payment or case-mix classification.
